subject: SLO runway check & GPU homework for dedicated pilot
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane@novus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO runway check & GPU homework for dedicated pilot

Jane — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + the items we need to validate for a Dedicated pilot so the internal teams can size GPU reservations correctly. I captured what we heard; please correct anything that’s off and drop the sample payloads where noted.

Key SLO targets (as-discussed)
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for 256 tokens; p95 <= 350ms for 1024 tokens (streaming allowed as fallback)
- Throughput: sustained 25–35 requests/sec (rps) for async batching windows; burstable to 120 rps for short spikes
- Concurrency: typical 40 concurrent streams, peak 90 concurrent (1% tail)
- Streaming: ~65% of user interactions should be streamed chunked responses (low-latency first-token important)

Data & artifacts we need from Novus to run an accurate pilot
1) 2–3 representative JSON payloads (prompt + metadata + avg token counts) — attach as sample_payloads.json
2) Expected distribution: percentage of short (<=64 tokens), medium (65–512), long (>512)
3) Typical session durations and ratio of streaming vs non-streaming calls
4) Any hard SLAs for first-byte (e.g., first chunk <120ms) or p50/p95 that differ from above
5) Compliance notes: are there any retention/inspection constraints for request logs?

What Redwood will deliver for the pilot (high-level)
- Dedicated pool recommendation: GPU type(s) + counts mapped to your sustained and peak targets
- Validation runbook: throughput, concurrency, and streaming experiments we’ll run (3 days of tests)
- Cost estimate for reserved throughput + burst policy
- Actionable tuning: batching window, KV cache warmup, quantization guidance

Attachments: novus_slo_workbook.xlsx (please fill sample payloads sheet) and streaming_slo_diagram.png

Next steps
- If you can drop sample payloads and distribution by end of this week, Ben and I will run a quick back-of-envelope GPU mapping and send a recommended config by Friday.
- Proposed window for validation tests: Sep 21–23.

Thanks — Hannah

Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers are in the right ballpark. Couple clarifications from our side:

- Our p95 target is more aggressive for short responses: p95 <= 150ms for <=128 tokens (we care about snappy search-style results)
- Streaming: closer to 70% of volume during peak product usage (desktop app), 40% during batch processing windows
- Typical payloads: average input tokens = 80, output tokens = 120; 95th percentile output tokens = 900
- Retention: we can share truncated logs for the pilot; full logs live in our VPC for compliance (SOC2 in process)

I attached two sample payloads inline below and uploaded a zip to our S3 (link in the Shared Drive doc). Also attaching a small CSV with session-length distribution.

Sample payload (short):
{"prompt": "Summarize the experimental results for Q2", "metadata": {"user_tier": "pro", "context_tokens": 60}}

Sample payload (long):
{"prompt": "Draft a 9-paragraph analysis of model drift over the past year", "metadata": {"user_tier": "enterprise", "context_tokens": 720}}

We’re okay with the Sep 21–23 window. Please include an estimate of what reserve (monthly committed) looks like vs. pay-as-you-go for the pilot period.

— Jane

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO runway check & GPU homework for dedicated pilot

Hannah / Karthik — quick internal note after reading Novus payloads and session CSV. High level GPU mapping thoughts (back-of-envelope):

- Workload shape: heavy short/medium tails but with meaningful long-output tail (up to ~900 tokens). Streaming-first (70% peak) means we need GPUs with strong kernel-level latency for small batches and good memory for long-token KV cache.

- Short recommendation: H100 80GB (FP16/TF32) gives best single-stream latency at small batch sizes; A100 80GB still solid and cheaper for reserved pricing if Novus is okay with slightly higher single-token p95 (~10–20% higher in our past tests).

- Quantization: consider INT8 or 4-bit on long-output paths to increase density for batch throughput tests — but validate QA on quality-sensitive prompts. We'll include both in the runbook.

- Sizing sketch (sustained 30 rps, 40 concurrent streaming): estimated dedicated pool = 3x H100-80 (pool with autoscale headroom to add 1–2 cards for bursts). For A100-80 reserved plan, plan = 4x A100-80. These numbers assume optimized batching (aggregate window 25–50ms) and prefix caching.

- Test plan items for pilot: p95 latency sweep across token lengths; concurrent streaming ramp (1–100); burst simulation to 120 rps; quantized vs baseline quality eval on ~100 prompts.

I’ll draft a short table mapping GPU count -> expected sustained rps and p95 and attach to the pilot doc.

Will follow up with the cost delta for H100 vs A100 reserved pricing.

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jane — appreciate the quick turnaround and the sample payloads. Ben and I sketched an initial config and a short test plan (link in related_links). High level next steps:

1) Novus sends any additional edge-case prompts (especially those that must preserve exact wording) by EOD Sep 10
2) Redwood will provision a temporary pilot pool (H100 3-node candidate + A100 4-node candidate) in our dev region for the Sep 21–23 window
3) We’ll run the tests Ben listed and produce a short decision memo: recommended GPU type, reservation size, expected monthly committed cost, and a fallback plan if the quantized path causes unacceptable quality regressions

Could you confirm the team who should receive the decision memo (ops, platform, procurement)? Also — if procurement wants preliminary numbers for an internal PO, Ben will include range estimates in the memo.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.
